_about: Every version of the portal, newest first (UPG-373). The top entry is the version of this code; shown at /whats-new and in the footer. A new entry starts after each deploy; until then every finished item goes into the top entry. 'revision' is the Cloud Run revision it went live as ('' until deployed).

releases.title: Jersey numbers up to 999
notes: A player's jersey number can have up to three digits (0 to 999), on the registration form and the Edit page.

releases.title: The kabaddi league by the PKL's rules
notes: Kabaddi leagues can use PKL Season 12 points: 2 for a win, 0 for a loss, and no ties. A level match goes to a tie-breaker of 5 raids each, then a golden raid, scored on the scorer's phone or typed on the tournament page.

PKL mode: the scorer taps how each raid ended and the portal works out the points, all outs, revivals, do-or-die raids, super tackles, time-outs and whose raid it is. The organiser can turn it off and score point by point.
The big screen shows the college logo and a QR code; the audience scan it to follow the live scores on their phones. Shared links show the college logo.
Scores show the moment the scorer taps, and the scoreboard and big screen update every one to two seconds.

A sports team uploads its logo and gives every player's jersey number when it registers. The logo shows beside the team's name on the scoreboard, the big screen and the fixtures; the jersey number beside each player's name.
The fixtures page opens with Choose a pool: All, Pool A or Pool B, with each pool's teams and their logos. A pool shows only its own table, matches and players' points.
The scoring page shows How to score this match. Only the event's SPOC and its coordinators can score.
Line-ups: before the start the scorer taps each team's seven starters by jersey number and name. The other players are the substitutes.

The scorer taps players, no lists: the raider, then the defenders he touched or the one who tackled him, then how the raid ended. Substitutions are by tapping too. The portal keeps who is on the mat and who is out, by name.
The match page leads with the score, then each team's players on the mat and out by jersey number, who is raiding now, and raid by raid with the scorer's name.
Full time names the player of the match; the scorer can change it.
Every match has a score sheet (PDF) to download, with the line-ups, each half's points, the result and lines for the officials' signatures.
Sports players can give their date of birth, and kabaddi players their position (Raider, Defender or All-rounder).
Find a player: search by name, and see their profile with team, jersey number, position, age, every match's points and their achievements. The date of birth, email and phone are never shown.
The points table explains P, W, T, L, SD and Pts, and why kabaddi uses the score difference instead of a run rate.
A team's registration form can ask each player's jersey name, separate from the full name: the organiser chooses Don't ask, Optional or Required.

releases.title: Kabaddi match day
notes: In a sports event the team is confirmed as soon as the lead registers: the players get no email to confirm. The organiser can still turn member confirmation on.
The SPOC sets which teams play each match from an Excel or CSV fixture sheet, along with dates, times and venues.
A big screen for a monitor or projector follows the match being scored, with the pool tables, the road to the final and the top players; no login, it refreshes by itself.
A map of the road to the final (semi-finals, final, champion) on the tournament, fixtures and big-screen pages.
A match can be postponed and put back on; every player's points are listed team by team on the fixtures page.

releases.title: A kabaddi premier league with pools and a button for every score; marking teams present after the event; pages that fit a phone
notes: After the event the SPOC can mark present a team that wasn't on the entry list or was out after a round, once they confirm it came; the portal records that the list was overridden.

On a phone the admin's events and users lists are cards that fit the screen, the dashboard's numbers take three short rows, the SPOC's console opens with a heading, and coordinators' event cards without a picture start with a thin band.
Every box on the tournament page says what it is for, for screen readers too.

A kabaddi or football league can have two pools with a table each, every pair can play twice (home and away), an inter-pool round counts in each team's own pool, and the semi-finals are 1st A v 2nd B and 1st B v 2nd A.
Matches are numbered M-01 onwards; the SPOC sets every match's date, time and venue from one spreadsheet file, and teams can have logos in the tables, fixtures and live scoreboard.
Coordinators open a sports event's matches and live scoring from their dashboard.

Live kabaddi scoring has a button for every score, two a row on a phone with both teams side by side: Raid +1 to +7, Bonus, Tackle, Super tackle, All out, Technical point, Out of bounds and Do-or-die failed.

releases.title: Sports tournaments run like a professional league
notes: Kabaddi tournaments: kabaddi points (5 for a win, 3 for a tie, 1 for a close loss), a league then playoffs, semi-finals, a final and a third-place match.
Live scoring on a phone: raid, bonus, tackle, all out and more, by player; anyone can watch the live scoreboard, which updates by itself.
Top raiders and top defenders, with Super 10s and High 5s, on the fixtures page.
Publishing a tournament's results gives the places, tells the teams and owes position certificates.

Every tournament mistake is fixed on the page, without help: clear a wrong result, reopen a match ended too early, remove any wrong point, walkovers, withdraw or bring back a team, rename, replace or add a late team, change a match's teams, change the points rule, undo the playoffs, and publish corrected results.
Two courts finishing at the same moment both keep their result.
The SPOC gives one person the participation certificate by hand (for example a winner judged without a check-in).
A page listing every version of the portal and what changed (this page).
The coordinator's event cards say "Opens soon" for an event yet to start, not "Closed"; the card no longer has a Delete button.
On a phone, messages such as "Welcome back" show at the bottom, above the menu, instead of over the page's title.
On a phone every header button, the bottom menu, the sign-in page's controls and the category chips are big enough to tap.
Dates read "26 Nov 2026" on the event page, the admin's pages and the coordinator's cards.
Each ticket shows View ticket and a More button; Cancel sits apart under More, so it isn't tapped by mistake.
Prizes typed as a number show in rupees, such as ₹3,000.
On a phone the SPOC's round quick-actions button no longer covers the bottom menu.

The admin dashboard's recent activity says what happened in words, at the time in India, without sign-ins. Students are greeted by name, with a short campus banner. The home page shows the next 6 events and "See all events". Page names in the top bar are no longer cut; the SPOC's event header and the coordinator's figures say what is true.
A team named "Team Phoenix" reads "Team Phoenix" in its result email and on its ticket, not "Team Team Phoenix".

Check-in is open on every day of the event, by the time in India (it was only the first day). After the event the SPOC marks a team that came but wasn't scanned as present, from the scanner's list, and can then issue its certificates.

releases.title: Hackathon certificates for everyone who came
notes: At a two-day hackathon, one check-in is enough for the participation certificate.
The student's Certificate button shows the organiser's own design, as issued.

releases.title: Marks changed on the Round panel
notes: The SPOC changes each judge's mark on the Round panel too (read-only once results are out).

releases.title: Places, not scores
notes: Teams see only their place once results are out, never scores or judges' marks.
The SPOC changes any judge's mark in the ranking until results are published.
A running two-day event stays in the student's active tickets until its last day.
The phone menu's Results tab is now Certificates.

releases.title: Certificate fonts
notes: Each box of the organiser's own certificate design has its own font: one of eight included, or the organiser's own font file.
"Issue certificates" can issue only participation certificates.

releases.title: A newer AI model for scoring
notes: AI scoring uses a newer Gemini model and tries again when the service is busy.

releases.title: Choose your columns
notes: Every Excel and CSV download lets you choose the columns.
The SPOC deletes an update; the evaluators' marks upload is always on the page.
Claude can score submissions when its key is set up.

releases.title: Problem statement selection
notes: Teams choose a problem statement in a time the SPOC sets (a limit per problem, lock, reopen, extend, or the SPOC assigns one); the submission is for that problem.

releases.title: Rooms, feedback, evaluators and a steadier site
notes: Rooms: a draft only the SPOC sees, a final check, then Allocate final; teams of 3 and 4 kept apart or mixed.
Website feedback from every participant, in rounds.
Outside evaluators' marks send the top teams through; a finale every judge scores.
The certificate's QR code sits in the design's own scan-to-verify box.
The scanner lists everyone on a team and saves each person ticked.
The SPOC deletes one person or the whole waitlist, and finds people on it with a search.
Registrations list filters, sorting, a filtered download and a WhatsApp message.
The lead and the SPOC add an email for a member who has none.
Easier first pages, a leaderboard switch, and judges or AI for the submission round.
The site no longer runs out of database connections when busy.

releases.title: Team changes and a clearer SPOC panel
notes: After the deadline the SPOC lets teams add and remove members for a set time.
The SPOC's event panel shows what to do now first, every tool kept but grouped.
The SPOC adds a team by hand; a deleted team can come back.
Every team member can sign in.

releases.title: The waitlist
notes: The waitlist on the SPOC's page, with Accept and an email for the accepted.
Each event's ticket guidelines and support email.
Documents for teams; the lead adds members.

releases.title: A clear registrations table
notes: The registrations list is a clear table with Edit, Cancel and Delete.

releases.title: Correcting details
notes: The lead and the SPOC correct registration details; members see their team.

releases.title: The form people register with
notes: The form made while creating the event is the one people register with.
The export shows every detail; a backup email account.

releases.title: Certificate design and member logins
notes: The organiser's own certificate design.
Team members confirm and sign in; the SPOC cancels a team; the SPOC's own form; the entry list.

releases.title: The hackathon portal
notes: The hackathon portal: teams, problem statements, submissions, AI scoring, rounds, judging and results.
Multi-round competitions; the registration form as a full official page.
NAAC / AQAR reports from event data; an impact page.
WhatsApp messages; open events for students from other colleges; share cards.
Merit and special-mention certificates.

releases.title: First live version
notes: Events of every kind: created, reviewed and published.
Registration forms, tickets with QR codes, check-in by coordinators.
Judging, results and certificates that can be checked online.
Student, SPOC, coordinator, judge and admin pages.
